name: Dynamic DAG Execution Control
description: The persisted proposal-to-attempt lifecycle; readiness, evidence lifecycle and candidate disposition are orthogonal context projections with explicit invariants.

fencing_token.source_of_truth: graph, node, attempt, claim, lease epoch, schedule hash and payload hash identity

received.description: Untrusted proposal received as inert data.

validated.description: Schema and semantic validation succeeded at the named base revision.

pending_approval.description: Privileged operation awaits an approval bound to exact proposal, policy and base hashes.

admitted.description: Proposal is committed; readiness is derived from current journal facts.

claimed.description: A fenced lease and dispatch outbox record are committed atomically.

running.description: Worker is executing with the current lease epoch.

blocked_safe.description: Worker reached a durable safe boundary and its lease is inactive; retry or unblocking creates a new claim.

succeeded.description: Immutable successful attempt outcome; candidate disposition may later be promoted or superseded without changing it.

failed.description: Immutable failed attempt outcome; any retry is a new node linked by retry_of.

cancelled.description: Worker is quiescent, lease fenced/released and cancellation outcome is immutable.

expired.description: Lease expiry ended this attempt; late outputs are fenced and a retry is a new node.

guards.description: Record schema, evidence references, authority and semantic graph checks pass.
Operation is automatic or carries an exact still-valid approval, and base revision remains current.
Approver identity and exact proposal/policy/base hashes match.
Derived readiness is true and resources, provider, isolation and budget are claimable.
guards.expression: ready(node) and resources_claimable and provider_eligible and isolation_proven and budget_allows

guards.description: Authenticated cancellation names current base revision and a non-empty reason.
guards.expression: operator_authenticated and base_revision == current_revision and reason != ''

guards.description: Worker presents current fencing token and protocol metadata is schema-valid.
A journaled logical-time observation proves the matching active lease expired.
guards.expression: logical_tick_journaled and matching_active_lease and lease_deadline <= logical_tick

guards.description: Dispatch reconciliation classified a stable non-retryable protocol failure for the current claim.
Authenticated cancellation names current base revision and claim.
guards.expression: operator_authenticated and base_revision == current_revision and current_claim

guards.description: Graph/node/attempt/claim/epoch identity matches an active unexpired lease, and atomic DONE protocol plus required gates pass.
guards.expression: fence_identity_matches and lease_active_unexpired and protocol_success and hard_gates_pass

guards.description: Graph/node/attempt/claim/epoch identity matches an active unexpired lease.
Incremental commit boundary reached and worker is quiescent.
A journaled logical-time observation proves the matching active lease expired.
guards.expression: logical_tick_journaled and matching_active_lease and lease_deadline <= logical_tick

guards.description: Authenticated cancellation targets the current revision and the worker is quiescent after a durable boundary.
guards.expression: operator_authenticated and base_revision == current_revision and durable_boundary and worker_quiescent

guards.description: Block evidence is resolved, any pause has an authenticated journaled resume, and a new epoch/resources can be claimed.
guards.expression: block_resolved and (control_status != 'paused' or authenticated_resume) and next_epoch and resources_claimable

guards.description: Authenticated cancellation names current base revision and a non-empty reason.
guards.expression: operator_authenticated and base_revision == current_revision and reason != ''

invalid_transitions.reason: Schema and semantic validation cannot be skipped.
Approval must return through current-revision validation.
A fenced lease and dispatch outbox must be committed first.
An attempt is never reset; retries are new nodes.
A retry is a new node.
A retry is a new node.
A cancelled attempt cannot be revived.
Expired epoch outputs are fenced; retry uses a new node.
Late success from a stale epoch is rejected.
Unblocking requires a new fenced claim epoch.

invariants.description: The transactional GraphJournal is the sole writer of graph_revision and canonical execution/control state.
Every committed record is hash-chained; only an uncommitted partial tail is recoverable, while complete or mid-journal corruption fails closed.
journal_seq advances for every durable event; graph_revision advances exactly once only for accepted readiness/authority-affecting changes.

schedule_hash and audit_state_hash use schema-versioned canonical UTF-8 JSON with sorted object keys, defined list/set ordering, NFC Unicode, integer-only numbers, explicit null/absence rules and LF line endings; replay reproduces both byte-for-byte.
invariants.expression: canonical_encoding_version_pinned and replay.schedule_hash == recorded.schedule_hash and replay.audit_state_hash == recorded.audit_state_hash

invariants.description: Tracker/ratchet remain authoritative for human intent; execution imports pinned facts one-way and never writes intent back.
Static projection preserves the exact six fields, sorting, warnings and exit-code contract of plan_waves.py.
Readiness is a pure derived predicate, never independently mutable state.
Every exogenous scheduling input is an immutable event or content-hashed policy/observation; replay never queries live time, tracker, config or health.
Claim and dispatch-request outbox are atomic; recovery reconciles the outbox before issuing a new epoch.

All worker outputs and promotion/Git effects require matching graph, node, attempt, claim, epoch, schedule and payload identities plus an active unexpired lease; stale workers may leave bytes but cannot admit or promote them.
invariants.expression: accepted_effect implies fence_identity_matches and lease_active_unexpired and effect_authorized_for_bound_hashes

invariants.description: Attempt outcome and candidate disposition are orthogonal; promotion/supersession never rewrites terminal success or failure.
At most one candidate per group is promoted, selected under CAS from hard-gate-passing successful candidates with frozen independent verifier hashes.
Candidate fan-out is refused unless isolation covers worktrees plus repo-global refs/config/hooks, ports, databases, caches and other declared shared resources; git stash is forbidden.
invariants.expression: fanout implies isolation_proven and not stash_allowed

invariants.description: Pause and cancel become effective only at a durable safe boundary after the worker is quiescent and its lease is released or fenced.
invariants.expression: control_effective implies safe_boundary and worker_quiescent and lease_inactive

invariants.description: Provider routing is deterministic from pinned capabilities, health, budgets, evidence and policy, with explicit stable tie-breaks.
Escalation requires an objective evidence trigger; model self-confidence alone cannot escalate.
An artifact author and verifier must belong to different configured independence groups; absence fails closed.
The OpenRouter execution adapter is model-agnostic and no workflow/routing code hard-codes model or vendor strings.
Credentials never enter model-controlled argv, environment, prompt, task files, event metadata or logs; the helper is outside and uncallable from the model sandbox.
invariants.expression: secret not in observable_worker_surfaces and not model_can_invoke(helper)

invariants.description: Experiment pre-registration is ratchet-bound before the first run and fixes factorial arms, corpus/strata, metrics, budgets, tools, verifier, stopping and analysis rules.
Experimental arms use the same harness, sandbox, tools, verifier and budget policy except for explicitly randomized factors; causal claims never exceed crossed randomized cells.

Anonymous previews, including the currently configured Ox Alpha experiment arm, remain external-preview-tier absent public weights/license evidence; unusually high probe usage is a calibration risk and circuit-breaker input.

Static fallback preserves both the exact plan_waves.py projection contract and wave-barrier dispatch, gating and failure semantics; journal failure never silently becomes a dynamic or partial executor.
Candidate promotion scoring is identity-blind and Git publication can originate only from the winner-selected promotion outbox, never ordinary attempt success.
Experiment runs follow the preregistered deterministic blocked-randomization and interleaving schedule; causal language requires assignment-log compliance and stable identity treatment.
invariants.expression: causal_claim implies assignment_log_valid and temporal_blocks_interleaved and identity_protocol_satisfied

invariants.description: Every blocked_safe node has a journaled wake condition/deadline and eventually becomes reclaimable, cancelled or a diagnosed liveness failure under logical time.
